items.title: Delhi's Pollution Tripled Even Before Diwali: Farm Fires Caused Way More Pollution Than Vehicles
points: Delhi's air pollution had already turned dangerous before Diwali fireworks added another layer of smoke.

His analysis, published in The Times of India, examined readings from 59 continuous air-quality monitoring stations, weather observations and farm-fire information from two types of satellite.
CSE's November 11 assessment uses the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's Decision Support System, along with air-quality and farm-fire data.

Transport accounted for 52% of the pollution attributed to Delhi's local sources, not 52% of every particle measured in the city.

items.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border

District Collector Anie Jula Thomas inaugurated the district-level handover on Thursday (November 12) by presenting the draft roll of the Kollam Assembly constituency to representatives of recognised political parties.

The Collector confirmed that the respective Electoral Registration Officers have also handed over the draft rolls for the remaining 10 Assembly constituencies in the district to political party representatives.
According to the draft roll, the district has a total of 21,08,106 voters across 2,261 polling stations in its 11 assembly constituencies.
The roll also accounts for 19,993 senior citizens aged 85 and above, 15,750 first-time voters in the 18–19 age group, 19,084 Persons with Disabilities (PwD), and 7,878 overseas electors.
The public and political parties can submit claims and objections regarding the draft electoral roll until December 11, 2026.

items.title: ‘Bouma’ movie review: Despite familiar settings, an engaging gothic horror until the final fumble
points: Babu, the writer and director of Bouma, probably believes in the old adage of the journey being more important than the destination.
The destination, predictably, in this gothic horror is an old haunted bungalow where the film comes to a rather underwhelming, open-ended climax.
The mysterious happenings within the bungalow gives one a ‘been there, done that’ feeling, for the setting is familiar from numerous films.
However, the happenings outside, where the film spends much of its runtime, evokes much curiosity.
This is something the film manages to maintain almost until the last act.
Bouma takes off unhurriedly through the point of view of Celine (Revathy Sarma), a singer at a resto-bar, and her live-in partner Jacob (Sagar Surya), a food delivery worker.
For a film of this nature, jump scares are absent, so are excessively violent visuals, although some extreme violent acts are implied.
Despite its familiar settings, Bouma is a somewhat satisfying experience, if one can ignore the weak third act.

items.title: Karnataka HC rejects convict’s plea for concurrent sentences in murder and witness-threat cases
points: The High Court of Karnataka has dismissed a petition filed by a 29-year-old convict seeking to have his sentences in two separate cases, one for murder and another for threatening a witness in the murder case, run concurrently instead of consecutively.
Nagaprasanna passed an order rejecting the plea of Ramesh from Bengaluru, who is currently undergoing imprisonment.
The petitioner had sought directions under Section 427 of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) to the jail authorities to ensure that his two sentences ran concurrently.
